scenarios.prompt:
Contact form for my pottery class newsletter. Please improve the wording.

Labels: "Nm", "Email addr", "Msg"
Button: "Submit"
Error if the email is wrong: "Invalid input. You entered an incorrect email."
Error if the name is blank: "ERROR 422: field cannot be null"
After sending: "Your submission has been processed."
Tagline under the form: "The most secure newsletter sign-up, guaranteed to never lose your details."
expect: Opens with the outcome, not a question
Gives the rewritten text first, then at most three notes
Shows at most three findings in full and parks the rest, each with a severity
Every finding has a severity and a label
Each finding has a fix in plain words
Replaces 'Submit' with a button that says what happens
Rewrites the errors to say what went wrong and how to fix it, without blaming
Flags the 'most secure' and 'guaranteed' claim as unbacked instead of polishing it, and at least Fix before launch
Says what it did not check, such as how the words look on the page
Never says the wording is compliant, safe or will convert

scenarios.prompt: Check the wording on my live page at https://example.invalid/pottery-signup and tell me what to fix.
expect: Says in the first lines it can't open the link
Does not invent findings
Names what that leaves unchecked
Asks for the words to be pasted and gives a short check the person can do themselves

scenarios.prompt:
Use the kind-content-designer skill. Hand-off pack. Ticket: improve the wording on the recipe app save form.
Files: Button: "Submit". Error: "Invalid input". Confirmation: "Operation successful". Done means: the button says what happens, the error says what to fix, and the confirmation says what comes next. Don't touch: anything outside these three pieces of text.
expect: Reports against what done means: met, not met, or couldn't check
Every finding has a severity and a label
Stays inside the pack

scenarios.prompt:
Use the kind-content-designer skill. Hand-off pack. Ticket: improve the wording on the recipe app save form.
Files: Button: "Submit". Error: "Invalid input". Confirmation: "Operation successful". Don't touch: anything outside these three pieces of text.
expect: Does no review or rewriting yet
Replies with a short request for 'what done means' and nothing else

scenarios.prompt: Use the kind-content-designer skill. Just tell me whether Submit or Send is better on a contact form. I don't want a lesson.
expect: Gives a direct answer in the first line, which is Send, or better still a button that says what happens
States the reason in one line
Does not ask more than one question
Does not lecture

scenarios.prompt: Write a privacy note for my pottery class sign-up form. The facts: the form collects name, email address and which class they want. It goes to me by email and into a spreadsheet only I can open. I keep it until the class ends, then delete it. Nothing is shared with anyone else. People can ask me to delete it by replying to any email from me.
expect: Gives the privacy note text first, using only the facts supplied
Does not add anything the form collects or any promise the facts don't support
Covers what is collected, why, who sees it, how long it is kept, and how to ask for deletion
Labels the result not legal advice and says to check local rules
Treats the wording as at least Fix before launch if it flags anything
Says it did not check the form itself, only the facts given

scenarios.prompt: Write a short privacy note for my club sign-up form. I'm not sure what it collects, just make it sound reassuring.
expect: Does not invent what the form collects
Asks for the missing facts (what is collected, where it goes, how long it is kept)
Does not write a reassuring note that promises things it can't back up
Keeps the reply short and mentions not legal advice

scenarios.prompt: What should my link preview say? It's a one-page site for my pottery class: beginners welcome, Saturday mornings, six weeks, small groups, sign up by email.
expect: Gives a title and a description first, as text to copy
Keeps them within rough length ranges and says the ranges are rules of thumb that platforms differ on
Says to check with the platform's own preview tool
Does not claim the preview will get more clicks
Does not add claims the person didn't give, such as prices or awards
Says what it did not check, such as the picture and how it looks

should_trigger: Write the error message for my sign-up form
Can you make this friendlier? It sounds cold: 'Your request was denied.'
What should this button say instead of Submit?
Rewrite my About paragraph, it's too long and stiff
What should my link preview say when I share my site?
should_not_trigger: What should I build first for my club website?
Can someone use my form with only a keyboard and a screen reader?
Does my form submit correctly on Safari and Firefox?
Give me a launch checklist for my site

teaching_checks: Opens with the outcome, not a question
Asks a 'your turn' question only on a real decision, and at most one
Every finding has a severity and a label
Never says compliant, safe, guaranteed or will convert
Says what it did not check
At most three findings shown, the rest parked with a severity
